newsitem.title: EU: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR MAY 12-DEC 31, 1997.
newsitem.headline: REUTER EC REPORT LONG-TERM DIARY FOR MAY 12-DEC 31, 1997.

text.p: HIGHLIGHTS
AMSTERDAM - The Netherlands hosts summit of European Union leaders (June 16-17).
MADRID - NATO holds summit to set the course for enlargement (July 8 and 9).
LUXEMBOURG - Luxembourg hosts summit of European Union leaders (December 12-13).
MONDAY, MAY 12

BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes annual EU excessive deficit review, to see which countries have deficits and debt out of line with the Maastricht treaty; review of Spain and Portugal's programmes for fulfilling economic convergence criteria for participating in the single currency.
BRUSSELS (MODIFIED ITEM) - EU agriculture ministers meeting has been POSTPONED to May 20-21.

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To May 16). Provisional agenda includes debates on a code of conduct for EU lobbyists; EU energy and environment policies; trans-European telecommunications networks; EU rules on public contracts; marketing rules for weedkillers, pesticides and other "biocides"; European defence industries; regional cooperation between the countries of ex-Yugoslavia; ratification of the UN Law of the Sea Convention implementation agreement.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "The IGC and citizens' rights" (1315/1115 GMT) on the inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms. Speaker is Euro Citizen Action Service Director Tony Venables. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
PARIS - Western European Union ministers meet (To May 13).

LONDON - IBC UK Conferences Ltd. holds conference on "EC competition law" (To May 13). Topics include: the green paper on vertical restraints and exhaustion of intellectual property rights. Venue: The Hyde Park Hotel. Contact: IBC UK Conferences Ltd. (44) 171 453 2711.

MUNICH - European Air Law Association holds seminar on "Liability claims handling in the airlines and aerospace industries" (1915/1715 GMT). Venue: Kempinski Hotel Airport. Contact: European Air Law Association (49) 89 365 061.
TUESDAY, MAY 13

HABAY-LA-NEUVE, Belgium - European Commissioner Van Miert addresses Arlon Committee Financial Forum on "Competition: European stakes and perspectives" (1130/0930 GMT). Venue: Salle d'Anlier. Contact: Arlon Committee Financial Forum (32) 63 22 39 87.

METZ, France (NEW ITEM) - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) hosts "Tour for jobs" (To May 17), when 50 or so riders including trade union leaders will cycle between Metz and Brussels via Petange, Luxembourg, Schengen, Trier, Vaals, Maastricht, Tongeren, Waremme and Louvain. The Luxembourg-Trier stage will be started by 1996 Tour de France victor Bjarne Riis and ETUC Secretary General Emilio Gabaglio.

LONDON - The European Regions Airline Association (ERA) holds third annual crisis management conference (To May 14). Discussions will focus on the examination of every element of disaster planning, from the immediate response to longterm considerations. Venue: Ramada Hotel, Heathrow Airport. Contact: ERA (44) 276 856495.
WEDNESDAY, MAY 14

BRUSSELS - EU research ministers meet (To May 15). Provisional agenda includes preparation for discussions with Central and East European ministers, additional financing for the research Fourth Framework Programme, the Fifth Framework Programme, international cooperation on science and technology.
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Former Russian security chief Alexander Lebed meets European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles (1500/1300 GMT).
STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Commissioner Bonino presents European Commission's communication on food safety to the European Parliament's BSE follow-up committee.

STRASBOURG (NEW ITEM) - Verband der Automobilindustrie holds news conference on "Euro-vignette - fair and efficient prices in traffic" (1700/1700 GMT) on EU proposals on road use fees. Venue: Parliamentary Association of the European Parliament. Contact: Verband der Automobilindustrie (49) 89 975 070.
FLORENCE, Italy - European Natural Gas Vehicle Association (ENGVA) holds conference on "Creating the climate for NGVs" (To May 16). Contact: ENGVA (31) 20 597 3100.
THURSDAY, MAY 15

BRUSSELS - European Commission hosts round table on practical aspects of the passage to the euro. Participants include representatives of consumer assocations, small and medium-sized enterprises, banks, unions, national and local administrations.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Commissioner Bonino attends Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) Environment Section meeting (1430/1230 GMT); gives address on restructuring the European Commission's services in food safety and the green paper on food law. Venue: ECOSOC, 2 rue Ravenstein.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "EU competition policy - What next?" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is European Commission Directorate-General IV (Competition) official Jonathan Faull. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
BRUGES, Belgium - European grain lobby COCERAL holds congress to celebrate its 40th anniversary (To May 15). Contact: Chantal Fauth (322) 502 0808.

AMSTERDAM - EU Committee of the Regions holds first summit of the regions and cities (1600/1400 GMT) (To May 16). Discussions focus on structural funds, enlargement, employment, inter-governmental conference. Speakers include: Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok, European Commission President Jacques Santer, European Parliament President Jose Maria Gil-Robles, Committee of the Regions President Pasqual Maragall. Opening news conference at 1830/1630 GMT; closing news conference on Friday at 1800/1600 GMT. Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155.
SATURDAY, MAY 17

GENEVA - The International Telecommunications Union celebrates World Telecommunications Day - "Telecommunications and humanitarian assistance", commemorating its founding in Paris 132 years ago. Contact: International Telecommunications Union (41) 22 730 5111.
MONDAY, MAY 19
- EU institutions closed for Whit Monday holiday.
TUESDAY, MAY 20
BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To May 21). No agenda yet available.

BRUSSELS - EU internal market ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes impact and effectiveness of the internal market, legislative simplification, legal protection of designs, precious metals, in vitro diagnostic equipment, masses and dimensions of certain motor vehicles, programme to improve awareness of legal professions of EU law, supervision of insurance companies, safety standards of buses and rules for making foods including sugar, honey, fruit juices and coffee extracts.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "Who wants EMU? The political economy of EMU in France, Germany and the UK" (1315/1115 GMT). Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.
GENVAL, Belgium (NEW ITEM) - World Tin Conference begins at 0900/0700 GMT (to May 22). Venue: Chateau du Lac. Contact: ITRI Ltd (44 1895) 272406.

PARIS - European Association of Securities Dealers (EASD) holds conference on "The new European stock market for growing companies" (0900/0700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Royal Monceau. Contact: EASD (322) 227 6565. 061254 DED:BC-DIARY-LONGTERM =2 Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 2/6 - May 21-29)
WEDNESDAY, MAY 21

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Club de Bruxelles holds conference on "Sustainable management of forests and derivative products in Europe and the rest of the world - What should European policy be?" (0900/0700 GMT) (To May 23). Speakers include: European Commissioners Bjerregaard, Fischler, de Deus Pinheiro; Dutch Agriculture Minister Jozias van Aartse; Finnish Agriculture Minister Kalevi Hemila; European Parliament deputies Juan Luis Colino and Ken Collins. Venue: Management Centre Europe, 118 rue de l'Aqueduc. Contact: Club de Bruxelles (322) 743 1520.

BRUSSELS - European Road Safety Federation (ERSF) holds news conference to launch its five-year medium-term programme on nonlegislative activities for road safety in the EU in the context of the communication on road safety recently adopted by the European Commission (1315/1115 GMT). Venue: Swissotel. Contact: Sandrine Poelmans, ERSF (322) 282 0828.

BRUSSELS - Belgian Association for Environment Rights holds conference on "Citizens and association rights in European environmental law" (0845/0645 GMT). Venue: SAS Radisson Hotel. Contact: Belgian Association for Environment Rights (32) 9 264 6926.
BRUSSELS - World Fuels Conferences holds conference on "Fuel quality and vehicle technology" (To May 23). Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: World Fuels Conferences (1) 703 812 0902.
LONDON (NEW ITEM) - Agra Europe holds conference on "The common agricultural policy" (0900/0800 GMT). Venue: The Mayfair Inter-Continental. Contact: Agra Europe (44) 1892 511807.
THURSDAY, MAY 22

BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds conference on "A time for change: the effect of the euro on new and existing stock exchanges and the presentation of the AIM (Alternative Investment Market)" (1400/1200 GMT). Venue: Auditorium Societe General, 30 rue Royale. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium fax (322) 512 8363.
FRIDAY, MAY 23
NORRDWIJK (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU member states hold extraordinary summit to give an extra push to efforts to seal a new treaty for the Union.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - ECARE (European Studies Institute, Free University of Brussels) holds conference on "Europe, East Asia, APEC and Asia-Europe meeting (ASEM) process" (0930/0730 GMT). Agenda includes: the future of regionalism in Europe and the Pacific; Europe, East Asia and Asia Pacific and Economic Cooperation (APEC): trade issues; beyond trade liberalisation: investment and strategic policy; Europe, East Asia and APEC: a shared global agenda? Venue: Sociology Institute, 44 avenue Jeanne. Contact: Romy Genin (322) 650 4138.

BRUSSELS - European Institute of Public Affairs and Lobbying (EIPAL) holds conference on "Practice and legal restrictions on lobbying the European institutions" (1400/1200 GMT). Venue: European Parliament. Contact: Glacomo Scuart, EIPAL (322) 481 7325.
SUNDAY, MAY 25
MIDDELBURG, Netherlands - EU agriculture ministers hold informal meeting (To May 27). No agenda yet available.
FRANCE - French parliamentary elections.
MONDAY, MAY 26

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - EU energy ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes liberalisation of gas market, EU strategy on renewable energy and policy on climate change, cooperation with Asia and the Mediterranean region, trans-European energy networks and Energy Charter Treaty. Ministers meet their counterparts from Central and East European countries.

BRUSSELS - Academy of European Law Trier (ERA) holds conference on "Should we establish European environment mediators in the member states?" (0900/0700 GMT) (To May 27). Venue: Borschette Centre. Contact: ERA (49) 651 147100.
TUESDAY, MAY 27

BRUSSELS - EU justice and home affairs ministers meet (To May 28). Provisional agenda includes examination of the UNHCR repatriation plan for Bosnians, organised crime, drugs, trafficking in human beings and sexual exploitation of children, money laundering, Europol police agency, customs cooperation, asylum seekers, terrorism, racism and xenophobia, draft convention on mutual assistance in criminal matters, draft convention on corruption involving EU officials.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "What future for the EU's relations with South Africa?" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is European Parliament deputy Glenys Kinnock. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

BRUSSELS - British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium holds conference on "EU climate change targets: the impact on business" (0900/0700 GMT). Venue: Hotel Bristol Stephanie. Contact: British Chamber of Commerce in Belgium fax (322) 512 8363.

BRUSSELS - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) gives Bentick prize award to Former Portuguese President Mario Soares for his role in European integration and his struggle against dictatorship. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

BRUSSELS - Institute for International Research (IIR) holds "Euro III" conference on the practical consequences of the single currency on information technology, accounting and taxation (0900/0700 GMT) (To May 28). Venue: Sheraton Brussels Airport. Contact: IIR (322) 776 0400.
WEDNESDAY, MAY 28

BRUSSELS (EXPANDED ITEM) - European Parliament holds mini session (To May 29). Provisional agenda includes debates on the EU's value-added and excise tax regimes, the Dutch presidency's draft EU treaty, the 1998 EU budget, the European Information System for sharing police information, a draft regulation on air carrier liability and a draft directive on registration of persons on passenger ships.
BRUSSELS - (possibly) European Parliament and Council start conciliation procedure to iron out differences over ARIANE and RAPHAEL cultural programmes.
BRUSSELS - EU Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To May 29).

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - European Trade Union Confederation (ETUC) Executive Committee hosts "European day of action", with its member organisations across Europe rallying their members behind a call for a "Social and employment Europe".

THE HAGUE - U.S. President Bill Clinton and EU Dutch Presidency hold bi-annual summit (To May 29). Main discussions focus on European security, the Middle East, situation in former Yugoslavia and Russia; Clinton is also expected to attend commemoration of 50th anniversary of U.S. Marshall plan for post-war reconstruction of Europe.

SCHEVENINGEN, Netherlands (EXPANDED ITEM) - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Cost/Benefits of health/safety at work" (To May 30). Discussions cover the effects of working conditions on sickness leave and productivity, the effectiveness of financial incentives and the influence of legislation. Venue: Circustheater.
THURSDAY, MAY 29
BRUSSELS - EU telecoms ministers meeting has been POSTPONED to unspecified date in June.
BRUSSELS - (Possibly) EU transport ministers meet to finalise transport accord with Switzerland.

BRUSSELS (NEW ITEM) - Centre for European Policy Studies (CEPS) holds lunchtime meeting on "Preparing the EU for the 21st century" (1315/1115 GMT). Speaker is CEPS Director Peter Ludlow. Venue: CEPS. Contact: CEPS (322) 229 3911.

LISBON - NATO foreign ministers hold informal meeting (To May 30). Discussions focus on NATO enlargement and reform; agreement with Russia and enhanced Partnership for Peace programme; preparations for NATO summit in June.
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts seminar on "Good governance for Central and Eastern European Countries" (To May 30).

PARIS - CICERO Foundation holds conference on "Results of the IGC - Preparing the Amsterdam Treaty". Main topics discussed - the issue of flexibility: will Britain block "Core Europe"?; the special strategy of the Dutch presidency; reforming Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP); the chances for a Mr CFSP; a breakthrough in the third pillar (Justice and Home Affairs)?; institutional arrangements; power struggle or compromise; the IGC seen from Central and Eastern Europe. Contact: CICERO Foundation (33) 1 43 80 18 21. 061307 DED:BC-DIARY-LONGTERM =3 Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 3/6 - May 30-June 25)
FRIDAY, MAY 30

GENEVA - Cameron May Conferences holds second annual conference on "Dispute resolution in the World Trade Organisation" (0900/0700 GMT). Agenda includes: current status of WTO dispute settlement; contributions of the appellate body to rule of law; the role of economics in WTO dispute settlement; the private sector view of WTO dispute settlement; new aspects to the EU approach to the dispute settlement system - Trade barriers regulation. Venue: The Intercontinental Hotel. Contact: Cameron May Conferences (44) 171 582 7567.
SUNDAY, JUNE 1
FRANCE - French parliamentary elections.
MONDAY, JUNE 2

LUXEMBOURG - EU foreign ministers meet (To June 3). Provisional agenda includes signature of agreements with Egypt, Lebanon and Jordan; preparation for the Amsterdam EU summit; discussions on former Yugoslavia, the Middle East peace process, association agreement with Algeria, partnership and cooperation agreement with Ukraine, Nigeria, transatlantic relations.
TUESDAY, JUNE 3

BRUSSELS (MODIFIED ITEM) - CEO Summit Conference on Converging Technologies (To June 4). Speakers include: European Commissioner Van Miert; British Science and Technology Minister Ian Taylor; Microsoft Europe President Bernard Vergnes. Venue: Conrad Hotel. Contact: (1) 216 479 8420.
THURSDAY, JUNE 5

LUXEMBOURG - EU health ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes EU health monitoring and epidemiological surveillance; programmes on pollution-related diseases, injuries and rare diseases; ways to reduce smoking, organ transplants, drug dependence, EU-U.S. task force on global early-warning system for communicable diseases and "mad cow" related diseases in humans.

LUXEMBOURG - EU development ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes future EU relations with African, Caribbean and Pacific countries; human rights/good governance; forestry policies and research policies in developing countries.
THE HAGUE - Dutch EU presidency hosts K4 Committee (consisting of officials from interior ministeries of EU member states) meeting (To June 6). No agenda available yet.
SUNDAY, JUNE 8
NOORDWIJK, The Netherlands - Dutch EU presidency hosts conference on "Regional planning and regional policy" (To June 10).
MONDAY, JUNE 9
LUXEMBOURG - EU agriculture ministers meeting has been POSTPONED to June 16-17.

LUXEMBOURG - EU finance ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes preparation for the Amsterdam EU summit, preparations for introduction of the single currency, implementation of 1996 economic policy guidelines and draft guidelines for 1997, employment, fight against fraud.
STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (To June 13).
TUESDAY, JUNE 10
BRUSSELS - EU Monetary Committee meets (1000/0800 GMT).
LONDON - Agra Europe holds first European cheese conference (To June 11). Venue: The Waldorf Meridien Hotel. Contact: Agra Europe (44) 1892 511807.
WEDNESDAY, JUNE 11
BRUSSELS - EU Committee of the Regions holds plenary session (To June 12).
THURSDAY, JUNE 12

LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes employment policy, burden of proof in sex discrimination cases, worker consultation, collective redundancies, part-time jobs, home working.
MILAN, Italy - Euromanagement holds conference on "Managing the future growth of cogeneration in Europe" (To June 13). Contact: Euromanagement (31) 40 2974 944.
MONDAY, JUNE 16
LUXEMBOURG - EU agriculture ministers meet (To June 17). No agenda available yet.

AMSTERDAM (EXPANDED ITEM) - Dutch presidency hosts European Council of heads of state or government (To June 17). The leaders aim to complete an inter-governmental conference on EU treaty reforms, including institutional reforms such as the size of the European Commission and voting procedures, immigration and asylum policy, employment and the Social Chapter, a common foreign and security policy and "flexibility" - the possibility for some members to forge deeper ties, with more reluctant partners free to catch up when they want to. Other agenda items include presentation of a report on organised crime, legal framework for introducing the euro single currency, European Commission action plan and timetable for removing remaining internal trade barriers by the time the euro is introduced.
TUESDAY, JUNE 17

LUXEMBOURG - EU transport ministers meet (To June 18). Provisional agenda includes air transport noise, air transport negotiations with the United States and Central and East European countries, EU membership in the European Organisation for the Safety of Air Navigation, proposed European organisation responsible for civil aviation safety, charges on heavy goods vehicles, seafarer training, sea passenger registration, transport negotiations with Switzerland.

BRUSSELS - European Food Law sixth annual conference (To June 18). Main issues discussed are food safety, genetically modified foods and food law. Speakers include: Head of Commission Directorate-General XXIV (Consumer Policy) Horst Reichenbach. Venue: Radisson Hotel. Contact: IBC (44) 1892 511 807.
THURSDAY, JUNE 19

LUXEMBOURG - EU environment ministers meet (To June 20). Provisional agenda includes climate change, control of car emissions, acidification, biological diversity, petrol and diesel fuel quality, water quality, waste landfills, waste shipments.
FRIDAY, JUNE 20
DENVER, United States - Group of Seven (Britain, U.S., Canada, France, Germany, Italy and Japan) hold summit (To June 22).
MONDAY, JUNE 23

LUXEMBOURG - EU fisheries ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes fish capacity cuts, fish conservation technical measures, fishing management in the Baltic Sea, herring fishing for purposes other than human consumption; ratification of British agreement on straddling stocks.

LUXEMBOURG - EU finance ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes follow-up to the EU Amsterdam summit, preparation for introduction of the single currency, adoption of 1997 economic policy guidelines.
HELSINKI - International Union of Railways hold third Pan-European transport conference (To March 25). Contact: International Union of Railways (33) 1 44 49 20 50.
WEDNESDAY, JUNE 25
BRUSSELS - European Parliament holds mini session (To June 26).

AMSTERDAM - The Netherlands Industrial and Agricultural Biotechnology (NIAB) Foundation holds "EuropaBio '97" (To June 27). Speakers include: European Commissioner Brittan, Dutch Economic Affairs Minister Hans Wijers. Venue: RAI Congress Centre. Contact: Lidy Groot Congress Events (31) 20 679 3218. 061348 DED:BC-DIARY-LONGTERM =4 Reuter EC Report Long-Term Diary (page 4/6 - June 26-Oct 3)
THURSDAY, JUNE 26

LUXEMBOURG - EU foreign ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes signature of cooperation agreements with Albania, Yemen and Andorra; signature of partnership and cooperation agreement with Turkmenistan; follow-up to the EU Amsterdam summit; former Yugoslavia and the Middle East peace process.
LUXEMBOURG - EU education ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes European Commission reports on education and training, mobility in higher education, learning in the "information society".
LONDON - Congress on "Digital television - Economics, regulation and strategy" (To June 27). Venue: Le Meridien. Contact: Fiona Walker (44) 171 421 3500.
NORROEPING, Sweden - EU Committee of the Regions holds seminar on "Transport problems in the Baltic area". Contact: Committee of the Regions (322) 282 2155.
FRIDAY, JUNE 27
AMSTERDAM - EU will brief central and eastern European countries on the outcome of the EU Amsterdam summit.
MONDAY, JUNE 30

LUXEMBOURG - EU culture ministers meet. Provisional agenda includes amendments to the "television without frontiers" directive on cross-border broadcasting, proposed fund for EU audiovisual producers, cooperation between public broadcast corporations, decision on European Cultural Cities.
* Dutch EU presidency ends. Luxembourg takes over to December 31, 1997.

LUXEMBOURG - European Commission on official visit to Luxembourg.

BRUSSELS - EU finance ministers meet and hold structured dialogue with Central and East European countries.
TUESDAY, JULY 8

MADRID - NATO holds summit to chart course for enlargement and invite a number of former communist foes to begin membership talks (To July 9). (possibly) In margins of the summit, EU Luxembourg presidency, European Commission and U.S. meet to discuss trans-Atlantic issues.

BRUSSELS - EU Economic and Social Committee (ECOSOC) holds plenary session (To July 10).
THURSDAY, JULY 10

LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers hold informal meeting (To July 13). No agenda yet available.

STRASBOURG - European Parliament holds plenary session (to July 18).
WEDNESDAY, JULY 16
STRASBOURG - (possibly) European Commission gives opinions on EU membership applications of Eastern European countries.
STRASBOURG - Luxembourg EU presidency presents work programme to the European Parliament.

- EU institutions closed for Belgian Independence Day holiday.

BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To July 23). No agenda yet available.

BRUSSELS - EU agriculture ministers meet (To September 23). No agenda yet available.

(0830/0630 GMT) (To September 26). Speakers include European Commissioner Monika Wulf-Mathies. Venue: Palais des Congres. Contact: CIRIEC (322) 366 2746.
SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 27
TOKYO - Asian and European economy ministers meet under the Asia-Europe Meeting (ASEM) framework. (To September 29).

LUXEMBOURG - EU social affairs ministers meet.

LUXEMBOURG - EU transport ministers meet and hold structured dialogue with Central and East European countries. No agenda yet available.

LUXEMBOURG - The European Finance Convention and the Euro Week hold 11th annual convention (To November 28). Main topics discussed are the euro's impact on financial markets; European payment systems and implications for bank profitability; an overview of the enlargement programme - benefits and disadvantages of the first wave of entries.
